raw_segments.text: of Thrasymachus.
If what they say is true, Socrates, since I myself am not of their opinion. But still
I acknowledge that I am perplexed when I hear the voices of Thrasymachus and myriads of
others dinning in my ears. And on the other hand, I have never yet heard the superiority
of justice to injustice maintained by anyone in a satisfactory way. I want to hear justice
praised in respect of itself. Then I shall be satisfied, and you are the person from
whom I think that I am most likely to hear this. And therefore I will praise the unjust
life to the utmost of my power, and my manner of speaking will indicate the manner in which
I desire to hear you too praising justice and censuring injustice. Will you say whether
you approve of my proposal?
